{
  "schema": "recallweave-nfa-blind-question-sheet/1",
  "contract_sha256": "0d4bf65fc8928f78faef71e0b61850e1903b67fe5a147ecb58c61da88e294846",
  "definitions": "All machines use alphabet {0,1}. An omitted edge is absent; each item specifies its epsilon edges. State sets are mathematical sets. Questions concern acceptance after all input is consumed. This sheet intentionally excludes answer indices and explanations.",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "nfa-01",
      "concept": "Branching paths",
      "prerequisites": [],
      "prompt": "An ε-NFA reads the entire word 01. One possible path consumes both symbols and ends in an accepting state; every other possible path rejects or stops early. What is the result?",
      "options": [
        "Reject: every path must accept.",
        "Reject: accepting and rejecting paths cancel.",
        "Accept: one fully consuming accepting path is enough.",
        "Undefined: an NFA must choose exactly one path in advance."
      ],
      "transfer": "Explain why counting the accepting paths is unnecessary for this accept/reject decision, and why a path that leaves input unread is insufficient."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-02",
      "concept": "Branching paths",
      "prerequisites": [],
      "prompt": "The current active set is {q0,q1}. On input 1, q0 has no destination and q1 reaches q2. There are no ε-edges. What is the next active set?",
      "options": [
        "{q2}",
        "∅, because one branch stopped",
        "{q0,q1,q2}",
        "{q0,q2}"
      ],
      "transfer": "Change q1 so it also has no 1-destination. What is the next active set, and can later input revive it without any active state?"
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-03",
      "concept": "Branching paths",
      "prerequisites": [],
      "prompt": "Start at q0; only q2 accepts. There are no ε-edges. q0 on 0→{q0}, on 1→{q0,q1}; q1 on 0→{q2}, on 1→∅; q2 has no symbol destinations. Does the machine accept 101?",
      "options": [
        "Yes, because the prefix 10 reached q2.",
        "Yes, because q0 remains active.",
        "No, because any branch that stops makes the whole word reject.",
        "No: after all three symbols the active set is {q0,q1}, with no accepting state."
      ],
      "transfer": "Trace the same machine on 1010. State the final active set and decision; explain how it differs from 101."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-04",
      "concept": "Epsilon closure",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Branching paths"
      ],
      "prompt": "The only ε-edges are q0→q1, q1→q0 and q1→q2. What is the ε-closure of {q0}?",
      "options": [
        "{q1}",
        "{q0,q1,q2}",
        "{q0,q1}, because a cycle prevents further search",
        "An infinite set, because the cycle can be repeated"
      ],
      "transfer": "Why can a visited-state traversal stop even though there are infinitely many walks around the q0–q1 cycle?"
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-05",
      "concept": "Epsilon closure",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Branching paths"
      ],
      "prompt": "A machine contains several ε-edges and an accepting state. What is the ε-closure of the empty active set ∅?",
      "options": [
        "All states with an ε-edge.",
        "All accepting states.",
        "∅: no starting state exists from which to follow an edge.",
        "The closure of the machine's original start state."
      ],
      "transfer": "Contrast closure(∅) with closure({q}) when q has no outgoing ε-edge."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-06",
      "concept": "Epsilon closure",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Branching paths"
      ],
      "prompt": "Start at q0; only q2 accepts. The only symbol edge is q0 on 0→q1, and the only ε-edge is q1→q2. After reading the word 0, which closed active set and decision are correct?",
      "options": [
        "{q1,q2}; accept",
        "{q1}; reject",
        "{q2}; accept, with q1 removed because it has an ε-edge",
        "{q0,q1,q2}; accept"
      ],
      "transfer": "Why must the simulator close the destinations after a symbol move? What is the result for the empty word in this machine?"
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-07",
      "concept": "Subset states",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Epsilon closure"
      ],
      "prompt": "An ε-NFA starts at q0, with ε-edges q0→q1 and q1→q2. There are no other ε-edges. What is the start state of its subset-construction DFA?",
      "options": [
        "The single state q0.",
        "The set of all accepting states.",
        "∅ until the first symbol is read.",
        "The subset {q0,q1,q2}."
      ],
      "transfer": "If only q2 is accepting, does this start subset accept the empty word? Explain without consuming a symbol."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-08",
      "concept": "Subset states",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Epsilon closure"
      ],
      "prompt": "The NFA accepting set is {q2}. Its reachable subset DFA contains a state whose members are {q0,q2,q3}. How is that DFA state classified?",
      "options": [
        "Rejecting, because not all members accept.",
        "Accepting, because at least one member is q2.",
        "Accepting only if q2 was entered without an ε-edge.",
        "Neither accepting nor rejecting until one member is chosen."
      ],
      "transfer": "Give one accepting and one rejecting subset for the same NFA accepting set. Explain why the number of rejecting members is irrelevant."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-09",
      "concept": "Subset states",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Epsilon closure"
      ],
      "prompt": "The subset construction reaches the empty subset ∅. What are its destinations on 0 and 1, even if the original NFA contains ε-cycles?",
      "options": [
        "Both destinations are ∅.",
        "Both destinations are the original start closure.",
        "Each destination is an arbitrary accepting subset.",
        "The transitions are undefined, so the constructed DFA cannot be complete."
      ],
      "transfer": "Is ∅ necessarily reachable in every subset construction? Distinguish the full power set from the subsets reached from the start."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-10",
      "concept": "Language preservation",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Subset states"
      ],
      "prompt": "An ε-NFA has five states. What can be concluded about the number of reachable states in its subset-construction DFA?",
      "options": [
        "Exactly five.",
        "Exactly 32.",
        "At most 32; some subsets may be unreachable.",
        "Unbounded, because ε-cycles permit arbitrarily long walks."
      ],
      "transfer": "Construct a five-state NFA whose only reachable subset is {q0}: specify its start, symbol moves from q0 and relevant ε-moves. What happens to the other four states?"
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-11",
      "concept": "Language preservation",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Subset states"
      ],
      "prompt": "Why does the full reachable subset construction recognize the same language as its ε-NFA?",
      "options": [
        "It agrees on every word shown in a finite test panel, which proves all future words.",
        "For every prefix, its DFA state equals the ε-NFA's closed active set; this invariant extends by each symbol and gives the same final acceptance.",
        "It merges all states that have the same accepting flag.",
        "It selects a single successful NFA path before reading the input."
      ],
      "transfer": "State the invariant for the empty prefix and explain one inductive step. Why do agreement checks only through length eight provide tests rather than the whole proof?"
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-12",
      "concept": "Language preservation",
      "prerequisites": [
        "Subset states"
      ],
      "prompt": "An NFA has no ε-edges. Both q0 and q1 accept; q0 is the start, both symbol moves from q0 go to q1, and both moves from q1 loop to q1. Reachable subset construction yields {q0} and {q1}. Is this necessarily a minimal DFA?",
      "options": [
        "Yes: reachable subset construction always minimizes.",
        "Yes: different subset labels always mean different future languages.",
        "No: minimization would require preserving the original two state names.",
        "No: one accepting state looping on both symbols recognizes the same language."
      ],
      "transfer": "Which language does this machine recognize, including the empty word? Separate eliminating unreachable subsets from merging equivalent reachable states."
    }
  ]
}

{
  "schema": "recallweave-enfa-independent-blind-solution.v1",
  "question_sheet_sha256": "1c39732eb75b10b53de90d24cabb633527c24151675ec9af928355d583105c89",
  "independent_contract_sha256": "30c028518bf8e2256c8ddb13960c276241b6e7b78eef18d67848aa1e039773a4",
  "scope": "Authored before exposure to answer keys, explanations, candidate model/source or outcomes. Mathematical/content review only, no native/browser or learning-outcome acceptance.",
  "public_contract_revisions": "Public behavior was read from v1 8de21369; question sheet binds v2 0d4bf65f. Producer reports only timestamp/provenance change; exact comparison remains pending.",
  "answers": [
    {
      "id": "nfa-01",
      "letter": "C",
      "answer_index": 2,
      "reason": "Acceptance is existential over paths that consume the whole input. The stated fully consuming accepting path decides the result.",
      "transfer_solution": "Accepting-path multiplicity does not change an existential yes/no result. A path with unread input has not recognized the complete word, even if its current state accepts."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-02",
      "letter": "A",
      "answer_index": 0,
      "reason": "The union of the two branches' destinations is empty union {q2}, namely {q2}. A stopped branch does not cancel a live branch.",
      "transfer_solution": "If q1 also has no 1-destination, the next active set is empty. With no active state, later symbol moves and epsilon closure remain empty; the original start is not silently reintroduced."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-03",
      "letter": "D",
      "answer_index": 3,
      "reason": "The successive sets are {q0}, {q0,q1} after 1, {q0,q2} after 10, and {q0,q1} after 101. Only q2 accepts, so 101 rejects.",
      "transfer_solution": "One additional 0 moves {q0,q1} to {q0,q2}, so 1010 accepts. Acceptance of a prefix cannot substitute for consuming the entire word; branches stopped at q2 on the next symbol do not kill the continuing q0 branch."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-04",
      "letter": "B",
      "answer_index": 1,
      "reason": "Zero epsilon moves retain q0. Reachability through q1 adds q1 and q2. The q1-to-q0 edge adds no new state.",
      "transfer_solution": "There are infinitely many walks around the cycle but finitely many states. Marking each visited state means its outgoing epsilon edges need exploration only once."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-05",
      "letter": "C",
      "answer_index": 2,
      "reason": "The epsilon closure of a set is reachable from its members by zero or more epsilon moves. An empty set supplies no initial member.",
      "transfer_solution": "closure(empty) is empty. If q has no outgoing epsilon edge, closure({q}) is {q}, since zero moves include the seed itself."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-06",
      "letter": "A",
      "answer_index": 0,
      "reason": "After the 0 edge the raw moved set is {q1}; its epsilon closure is {q1,q2}. Since q2 is in the final set, the word 0 accepts.",
      "transfer_solution": "Closing after a symbol includes the valid zero-input continuation from q1 to q2 while retaining q1. For the empty word the closed start set is {q0}; q0 has no epsilon edge and is not accepting, so the empty word rejects."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-07",
      "letter": "D",
      "answer_index": 3,
      "reason": "The subset DFA starts in the full epsilon closure of q0, which is {q0,q1,q2}. This is one DFA state whose identity is an NFA-state subset.",
      "transfer_solution": "If only q2 accepts, the start subset is accepting because it contains q2. Therefore the empty word accepts without consuming any alphabet symbol."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-08",
      "letter": "B",
      "answer_index": 1,
      "reason": "The subset is accepting because its intersection with the NFA accepting set {q2} is nonempty.",
      "transfer_solution": "For example {q2} accepts and {q0,q3} rejects, as does the empty subset. Extra nonaccepting members cannot invalidate the existence of an accepting member."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-09",
      "letter": "A",
      "answer_index": 0,
      "reason": "Both symbol moves from no states yield the empty union; epsilon closure remains empty. Hence the empty subset self-loops on 0 and 1.",
      "transfer_solution": "The empty subset need not be reachable: a one-state NFA whose state loops on both symbols never reaches it. The power set lists possible subset identities; a reachable construction retains only those discovered from the closed start."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-10",
      "letter": "C",
      "answer_index": 2,
      "reason": "A five-element set has 2^5=32 subsets, and every constructed state is one such subset. Reachability can reduce this number.",
      "transfer_solution": "Choose start q0, zero(q0)={q0}, one(q0)={q0}, epsilon(q0)=empty. Give q1..q4 no incoming edge from any reachable state; for example make all their edge sets empty. Then the only reachable subset is {q0}. The four other declared states remain unreachable, regardless of their accepting flags."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-11",
      "letter": "B",
      "answer_index": 1,
      "reason": "The active-set invariant connects every finite input prefix to the DFA's current subset and therefore connects final acceptance for every word.",
      "transfer_solution": "Base: before input, both current representations are the epsilon closure of the NFA start. Step: if the current sets agree, take the union of destinations on the next symbol, then epsilon-close; this is exactly the constructed DFA transition. Acceptance is the same nonempty intersection with F. Testing through length eight checks finitely many instances, not the unbounded set of all finite words."
    },
    {
      "id": "nfa-12",
      "letter": "D",
      "answer_index": 3,
      "reason": "Both reachable subset states accept and every continuation remains accepting. A single accepting state with two self-loops recognizes the same language.",
      "transfer_solution": "The language is all finite binary words, including the empty word. Removing unreachable subsets cannot remove either {q0} or {q1}, because both are reachable. Minimization instead merges reachable states with identical future acceptance behavior."
    }
  ],
  "ambiguities": [],
  "summary": "All twelve items have one mathematically correct option under the explicit whole-word, absent-edge and set conventions. All transfer prompts admit a clear answer without changing those conventions.",
  "proof_scope": "The invariant is the all-finite-word proof; individual examples and bounded computational tests are separate evidence.",
  "references": [
    "https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~aho/cs3261/Lectures/L2-Finite_Automata.html",
    "https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~aho/cs3261/Lectures/L3-Regular_Expressions.html"
  ]
}
